I can’t help with instructions for carrying out attacks or compromising systems.
What I
can
do is explain how SQL injection works at a high level and how to prevent it—this is useful if you’re building or securing a website:
What SQL injection is (high-level)
SQL injection happens when an application includes unsanitized user input in a database query. An attacker can manipulate that input so the database executes unintended commands.
Common causes
Concatenating raw user input into SQL queries
Lack of input validation or sanitization
Overly permissive database permissions
Detailed error messages revealing query structure
How to prevent it
Use parameterized queries (prepared statements)
This is the most effective defense.
Use ORM frameworks
that automatically handle query parameterization
Validate and sanitize inputs
(e.g., enforce types, lengths, formats)
Least-privilege database access
(don’t use admin credentials in apps)
Escape inputs
when parameterization isn’t possible (last resort)
Disable detailed error messages
in production
Web application firewalls (WAFs)
can help detect/block attacks
Example (safe vs unsafe)
Unsafe (vulnerable):
SQL
SELECT
*
FROM
users
WHERE
username
=
'" + userInput + "'";
Safe (parameterized):
SQL
SELECT
*
FROM
users
WHERE
username
=
?;
